LESSON: OBLIQUE PROJECTION.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical studies.
Topic 2.1: Oblique Projection.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oblique Projection., part of Communication in Pre-Technical studies. in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How do you draw diagrams in oblique? How are oblique drawings used in the technical field?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oblique Projection. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: A learner develops speaking, listening and self-expression skills when brainstorming on the

characteristics of oblique drawings.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: A learner develops interpretation and inference skills by searching and exploring different options

of drawing three-dimensional diagrams in oblique.

Values:
• Responsibility: A learner enhances diligence as they care for the print and digital media as well as drawing instruments when

• learning how to draw three dimensional objects in oblique.

• Unity: A learner enhances cooperation with others as they use audio-visual aids in groups to search for information on and

• discuss characteristics of oblique drawings.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Creative Arts and Sports: A learner makes free-hand pictures of three-dimensional objects.·

• Visual Art: A learner makes free-hand pictures of three-dimensional objects.

• Mathematics: A learner makes oblique drawings to specific dimensions in technical drawing.

13

• English: A learner shares opinions, ideas and feelings while carrying out group activities.

Suggested learning resources:

• Three-dimensional wooden block.

• Plasticine or modeling clay.

• Digital devices with assistive technology.

14
